title: If a Leader Had Only One Question They Could Ask
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece argues that of all the questions a leader could ask, 'What do you think?' carries the most leadership weight because of what it signals about respect, humility, and openness. It explains how consistently asking for input builds trust, invites people to come prepared with their own views, and models that decisions are informed by more than just the leader's own conclusions. The article positions the question as especially powerful when asked of those with far less seniority or expertise, since it demonstrates that the leader values people over authority.
points: "What do you think?" is presented as the single most powerful question a leader can ask.
Asking it signals respect for others' knowledge and models openness rather than having all the answers.
Consistent use trains team members to come prepared with real opinions and builds trust over time.
Asking it of less experienced people is framed as a humility signal that builds team-wide trust.
quotes: But if a leader had only one question they could ask, the most powerful inquiry is “What do you think?
When a leader asks for input, it shows they respect the other party’s knowledge and perspective.
Leaders who ask for a view signal that they don’t have all the answers and have yet to land on a conclusion. This openness fosters trust.
By asking this question of those with far less expertise, experience, and skillfulness, leaders show a humility that builds trust within a team.
Of the many questions a leader might ask, “What do you think?” carries the most weight.
